text:
### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, activities A14, A15, A20, A21 and A22 were not observed at all (0 of 200 traces). In the later window, each of them runs in roughly 17–23 in 100 traces (A14 about 23, A20 about 22, A15 about 21, A22 about 18, A21 about 17 in 100), at most once per trace, around the middle of the trace (mean normalised position about 0.50). [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004]

- The five are mutually exclusive: in the later window, every pair among them shows only "one or the other" traces (for example, A14 without A20 in about 22 in 100 traces and A20 without A14 in about 22 in 100, both in the same trace in 0), so a later trace contains at most one of the five. [REL001, REL002, REL003, REL007, REL008, REL012]

- Earlier, A24 always passed flow directly to A25, and A25 always directly to A26. In the later window, about 52 in 100 of A24's outgoing transitions go to one of the five new activities (about 48 in 100 still go to A25), and about 48 in 100 of A25's outgoing transitions go to one of the new activities (about 52 in 100 still go to A26). Each new activity is followed by A25 or A26 in roughly even shares (for example, A14: about 53 vs 47 in 100). [DIR006, DIR007, DIR001, DIR002, DIR003, DIR004, DIR005]

- Ordering: whenever one of the new activities runs, A24 comes before it and A26 after it (for example, A24 before A14 in about 22 in 100 traces, and A14 before A26 in about 22 in 100). The new activity sits either between A24 and A25 or between A25 and A26: A14 and A25 co-occur in about 22 in 100 traces, with A14 first in about 12 and A25 first in about 11. [REL004, REL005, REL006, REL009, REL010, REL011, REL013, REL014, REL015]

- Distances: in every earlier trace, A26 followed A24 two positions later. In the later window, A26 follows A24 three positions later in about 199 of 200 traces, and the A24→A25 and A25→A26 distances each stretch from always 1 to 2 in roughly half the traces (about 52 and 48 in 100). Together this means exactly one event is inserted between A24 and A26 in nearly every later trace. [LAG001, LAG002, LAG003]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the hypothesis that in the later window one extra step is inserted between A24 and A26 in nearly every case: exactly one of five mutually exclusive alternative activities — A14, A15, A20, A21 or A22 — executes once, placed directly after A24 (before A25) in about 52 in 100 traces or directly after A25 (before A26) in about 48 in 100, with the choice among the five spread about evenly; earlier, this segment always ran A24 → A25 → A26 with nothing in between. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005, DIR006, DIR007, REL004, REL005, REL006, LAG001, LAG002, LAG003]

The change is shown directly by relational, successor and lag evidence rather than by participation alone: A24 and A25 redistribute about half of their outgoing flow to the new activities, A24 always precedes and A26 always follows them, and the A24→A26 distance grows from 2 to 3 positions in about 199 of 200 later traces — a comparison based on activities observed in all traces of both windows. The volume of qualified evidence also far exceeds what a stable process produces: 34 control-flow items qualified where about 0.44 would be expected by chance. [DIR006, DIR007, REL004, REL006, LAG002]

Limitations: with 200 traces per window, the evidence cannot show whether the five activities are genuinely new or were simply too rare to appear in the earlier sample, and it constrains only the segment around A24–A26, so behaviour elsewhere in the process cannot be checked. [OCC001, OCC002, OCC003, OCC004, OCC005]
